The Sanctuary

The Colonial Theatre

Hagerstown, Maryland

Transparency Notice

Fictional Location: The Colonial Theatre, as described within this archive, is a fictional setting existing entirely within the Fractured Prisms narrative universe. While it references the real-world geography of Hagerstown, Maryland, the events, architectural modifications, and subterranean vault described below are works of fiction designed to explore the band's immersive lore.

The Lesson of 1985

The 1985 Independence Stadium show was a monumental success, but it taught the siblings a terrifying lesson: you cannot control an environment of 100,000 screaming fans. The sensory overload and the sheer logistical terror of navigating Claire safely through the chaotic backstage labyrinth pushed Rhys to his breaking point.

They resolved to never perform in a stadium again. Using their immense generational wealth, they purchased The Colonial Theatre in downtown Hagerstown in cash just before it was slated for demolition. After a rigorous, three-year restoration, they transformed it into an absolute, hyper-controlled 1883 London bubble right in the middle of Maryland.

House Rules: The Performances

  • The 8:00 PM Curfew: Doors open at 7:00 PM. Performances begin precisely at 8:00 PM.
  • Duration: Sets last exactly 39 minutes. The show concludes at 8:39 PM. No encores.
  • The Standing Frame: Claire performs securely locked into a custom-machined standing frame hidden entirely beneath heavy, opulent 1883 mourning dresses.
  • The Sanctum Protocol: No press or chaotic VIP backstage access. The trusted Hagerstown theatre crew works collaboratively and respectfully with Rhys and Claire—keeping all ramps, lifts, and corridors clear while respecting that Rhys personally handles Claire's physical transfers and sensory recalibration.

The Shadow Architecture

Seamless accessibility hidden behind 1914 Baroque design.

The Auditorium Slope

The entire theater floor was ripped out and re-engineered into a gradual, imperceptible slope. All stairs were eradicated, creating flawless, seamless accessibility for public wheelchair users while maintaining the illusion of a traditional tiered theatre.

The "Birdcage" Elevator

Hidden behind the grand lobby staircase is a vintage mahogany and wrought-iron elevator. Secretly powered by state-of-the-art 1984 commercial hydraulics, it utilizes infrared safety sensors and laser-leveled magnetic locking so Claire's wheelchair never catches on a lip.

The Subterranean Vault

A lead-insulated, doorless vault built deep in the basement. It features a roll-in wet room, a kitchenette, and a bed built to the exact height of Claire's chair for zero-gravity transfers, allowing the siblings to completely isolate themselves from the outside world.

The Refreshment Room

The theatre enforces Her Majesty's English and strictly authentic British cuisine. To the locals in Hagerstown, it is the peak of British culture. To Rhys and Claire, it is a brilliant decoy, feeding the obsessive fans' illusion that the band is hiding somewhere in London.

Strict Medical Policy

NO ALCOHOL IS SERVED ON THESE PREMISES. Both Resident Directors take specialized medication that, when mixed with alcohol, induces severe respiratory distress. This is a dry venue. No exceptions.

Interval Menu

  • Proper Tea
    English Breakfast or Earl Grey. Milk offered, never forced.
  • Fish & Chips
    Served strictly in newspaper-style cones before the show.
  • Canary Creams & Digestives
    Traditional biscuits essential for tea service.
  • Dandelion and Burdock
    A traditional, slightly medicinal vintage soft drink.
  • Pork Scratchings
    A savoury, intensely crunchy pub snack.

Archivist's Addendum

Deciphering the 39-Minute Curfew

To the public, the strict 8:00 PM start time and the abrupt 39-minute duration appeared to be brilliant, eccentric artistic choices. In truth, they were absolute medical and technical requirements engineered for survival.

The Medical Limit: Claire’s custom standing frame allowed her to project vocal authority from beneath her Victorian dresses, but it was not a magical device. Being rigidly strapped into an upright, weight-bearing position put immense strain on her body. Thirty-nine minutes was the absolute maximum medical threshold her body could endure before the pain became intolerable and she risked physical injury.

The Analog Ceiling: Rhys’s massive wall of 1980s analog synthesizers and primitive step-sequencers were notoriously unstable. Under the heat of stage lighting, the analog oscillators began to drift. By the 40-minute mark, the entire mechanical orchestra would begin sounding dissonant and out of key. They ended the show exactly before the machines failed.

The Transit Window: Because the siblings relied on the Route 441 County Commuter bus from Williamsport, they arrived in Hagerstown in the mid-afternoon. The 8:00 PM start allowed Rhys five unhurried hours in a locked theatre to manually tune dozens of oscillators, test the hydraulic lifts, and safely transfer Claire into her standing frame without triggering a sensory meltdown. While the crowd dispersed peacefully into the quiet Hagerstown evening at 8:40 PM—bypassing noise complaints entirely—Rhys and Claire descended into the Subterranean Vault. Stranded until the Sunday buses resumed, they isolated themselves safely underground.

Engine Room Records (Real-World Imprint)
